clue.text: Hawking would reject this total placed inside

indicators.note: inside says one word is set within the letters of another

blocks.note: a total is a sum
placed means put

explanation.surface: It sounds like Stephen Hawking turning down some grand total of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawking is not the physicist: to hawk is to clear the throat noisily, and this is what such a person spits out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is the phlegm a person coughs up and spits out when clearing the throat.

clue.text: Indications of office sin, screwing around, gin swilling and editor getting end away

indicators.note: screwing around suggests twisting and mixing, so the letters before it are jumbled
swilling sloshes liquid about, so the drink's letters get stirred up
getting the end away means the last letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Ian Hislop is the editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle appears

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style tale of office misbehaviour: sex, booze, and an editor having his wicked way.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting your end away is British slang for having sex; here it simply drops the last letter of IAN to give IA, ending INSIGNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems worn to show someone's rank or official position.

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Urchins are scruffy, mischievous children, so the word stands for kids.

clue.text: Instrument bottle covering top of todger

explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord-like keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Call off row on date – it's a trendy thing

explanation.definitionFit: A buzzword is a fashionable word or phrase of the moment, hence a trendy thing.

clue.text: An arsehole during the elections

blocks.note: found running across the two words

clue.text: Top half of mouthy inmate of Celebrity Big Brother (God, this country!)

blocks.note: Jade Goody, whose loud remarks on the 2007 Celebrity Big Brother caused a race row
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: An exasperated aside about a loudmouth on a reality TV show, ending in a groan at the state of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of this long clue delivers just two letters. Celebrity Big Brother is a reality show in which celebrities live together in a house under cameras.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a country; 'this' points the reader to the answer itself rather than to Britain.

clue.text: Minister's device for easing an erection with rising growths

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upward, from bottom to top

blocks.note: a jack is a device for raising something heavy, such as a car
warts are small skin growths

explanation.surface: A smutty suggestion that a government minister owns a gadget to help with his erections.
explanation.walkthrough: The erection is anything raised, like a car on a jack. Jack Straw was a senior Labour cabinet minister, Justice Secretary in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Straw held several ministerial posts, including Home Secretary, Foreign Secretary and Justice Secretary.

clue.text: So, bursting to show one's protruding organ?

definitions.text: So, bursting to show one's protruding organ?

blocks.clueFragment: bursting to show one's protruding organ
blocks.note: surface reading: someone desperate to flash their private parts
setter's reading: a hernia, where an organ pushes through a torn muscle wall

explanation.walkthrough: The organ is not the one the surface suggests; it is an internal organ poking through a tear, and bursting is the tear itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruptured person has a hernia, a tear in the abdominal wall through which part of an organ protrudes.

clue.text: (& 12/27) Alex & co's North South coalition that's pisspoor do

indicators.note: pisspoor means dreadfully bad, so the letters before it are in a sorry jumble

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A sneer at a north-south political alliance as a miserable affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex is Alex Salmond, then leader of the Scottish National Party, which had just formed a minority government in Scotland in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex Salmond and his colleagues made up the party he led, so 'Alex & co' names it.

clue.text: Place down under, in another place down under, foreign article and end of tube?

explanation.definitionFit: Come, or cum, is a vulgar slang noun for ejaculated seminal fluid.

clue.text: Arthur exploded about "end of strike" piss-taker

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
exploded means blown apart, so the name's letters are scattered
about means around, so the jumbled name goes round the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Arthur losing his temper over the end of a strike, and someone mocking him.
explanation.walkthrough: A piss-taker is normally a mocker; here it is literally what takes away urine. Arthur suggests Arthur Scargill, the miners' strike leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The urethra is the duct that carries urine out of the body, read literally as piss-taker.

clue.text: He's at it again, the love rat!

explanation.definitionFit: A love rat cheats on a partner, seeing two people at once, which is what that hyphenated word describes.

clue.text: Like the bog awful army keeping quiet ...

keeping means holding in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: An army on the toilet trying to keep the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for the toilet, but here it is a stretch of wet ground. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy, waterlogged ground is marshy, so the adjective describes a bog.

clue.text: Our incumbent no longer against one getting buggy

blocks.note: v is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one
a buggy is a small light car

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye ran Tony Blair as the vicar of St Albion's parish; he resigned as prime minister in June 2007, so the vicar was 'our incumbent no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An incumbent is the priest holding a parish, and Private Eye's long-running parody made Blair the magazine's own parish priest.

clue.text: ... about rises in badly-cast provisions

explanation.definitionFit: To provision is to supply with food, and to cater is to supply food, so caters fits provisions.
